title: Security: Streaming & Management Console Modernisation
subtitle: Replacing green-screen configuration with a visual, policy-driven experience
description: Replacing green-screen configuration with a visual, policy-driven experience.
detailedSummary: The Security product line protects mainframe estates by streaming security-relevant data. The streaming product was configured through terminal panels, and the management console was widely seen as intimidating and complex. I led UX for the modernisation of both: web-based policy management, flow-map visualisation and a UX audit.
problemSpace: Green-screen configuration and intimidating management consoles made streaming setup complex and error-prone.
solution: A centralised, visual policy system: policies are created once, tagged, deployed to many instances and understood through an estate flow map.
keyOutcomes: Streaming web UX validated with 6 customers
role: UX leader for Security product line: streaming web enablement, console re-platform, policy management
teamComposition: Three designers (one at 50%) · Research: one UX researcher

leadershipPerspective.executiveMandate: Use customer evidence to make design decisions credible, protect quality when development moved ahead of design, and keep scarce capacity on highest-priority work.
leadershipPerspective.strategicRole: Supported UX audit to find usability gaps and design-system inconsistencies before development effort.
leadershipPerspective.crossFunctionalSynergy: Connected product management, R&D and design-system team early so design and engineering moved together.
leadershipPerspective.teamLeadership: Coached presenters and protected design files from last-minute unverified edits.
leadershipPerspective.orgTransformation: Transformed repeated terminal work into a streamlined, policy-driven web experience.

phase1Discover.overview: Phase 1: Discover & Empathize — Customer Pain Points & Workflow Mapping.

researchAnalytics.detail: Studied streaming product and console panel.

keyInsights: Terminal skills are a growing challenge in large environments.

phase2Define.coreProblemStatement: How might we let a systems programmer see, build and deploy a streaming policy across an entire estate with confidence?
jobsToBeDone: Build one policy and push it to every instance.
Show coverage and modification history to record owners.
phase2Define.mentalModelMisalignment: Configuring systems one by one rather than reasoning about policies and coverage across the estate.

phase3Ideate.northStarVision: Centralised, visual policy system with flow-map visualisation of running policies across all instances.

architecturalShifts.rationale: Removes repeated manual steps and maintains an audit trail.

strategicTradeOffs: Put clickable instance names on hold until scope was agreed; scaled for 100+ instances.

phase4Prototype.validationApproach: Streaming prototype for customer event (May 2025), concept tests and UX audit.

phase5Implement.governanceFramework: Bi-monthly cloud and security prioritisation reviews aligning UX and R&D.
phase5Implement.designSystemIntegration: Design-system portfolio lead involved for developer framework training.
phase5Implement.continuousFeedbackLoops: Customer recruitment and validation serving as model for other modules.

roiMetrics.label: Streaming UX Validated
roiMetrics.context: Lower design risk and customer-approved direction.

commercialBenefits: Reduced reliance on terminal skills in large environments.
businessOutcomesAndROI.operationalSavings: Focused capacity on highest-value customer and product management demand.

leadershipTakeaway: Enterprise security UX modernisation requires co-creation with customers and early alignment between design and engineering.

title: Agentic AI Experience
subtitle: Designing human-agent collaboration that customers can trust
description: Designing human-agent collaboration that customers can trust.
detailedSummary: As the company moved from AI chat to agents that can investigate and act on mission-critical mainframe systems, the experience question became: how much autonomy, shown how, with which safeguards? I led UX direction for that shift, from a cross-product AI experience framework to the November 2026 agentic release decisions and Agentic Workspaces programme.
problemSpace: Moving from AI chat to autonomous agents requires calibrated trust, transparent reasoning, and human-in-the-loop safeguards.
solution: Designed a two-axis framework (conversational/embedded and assistive/agentic), adjustable autonomy modes (Ask, Assist, Agent), and risk-proportional friction.
role: UX leader for agentic experience strategy and cross-product alignment (Platform, Ops and Data)
teamComposition: Assistant UX lead and three designers · Research: two UX researchers

leadershipPerspective.executiveMandate: Agentic UX is a leadership problem before it is a design problem—turning open debates into recorded decisions.
leadershipPerspective.strategicRole: Authored end-to-end UX plan for Workspaces, phases, roles, and undated milestones.
leadershipPerspective.crossFunctionalSynergy: Facilitated cross-product alignment across Platform, Ops, and Data.
leadershipPerspective.teamLeadership: Proposed four big rocks in the AI initiative discussion and invited owners.
leadershipPerspective.orgTransformation: Reframed AI chat as a progression from chat to workflows to workspaces.

phase1Discover.overview: Phase 1: Discover & Empathize — Customer Evidence on AI Trust, Maturity & Incident Workflows.

phase2Define.coreProblemStatement: How might we let customers delegate more to agents over time while keeping approval visible?
phase2Define.mentalModelMisalignment: Individual product agents without suite-level workflow continuity.

phase3Ideate.northStarVision: Agentic workspaces: persistent shared workspaces where humans and agents coordinate.

architecturalShifts.rationale: Gives psychological safety and graduates confidence.

strategicTradeOffs: Hidden unlicensed AI features rather than greyed-out options.

phase4Prototype.validationApproach: Two tracks: November 2026 release interaction rules and Agentic Workspaces validation.

phase5Implement.governanceFramework: AI Experience Framework for naming, licensing, and failure behaviors.
phase5Implement.designSystemIntegration: Assistant identity and action-naming rules in design system.
phase5Implement.continuousFeedbackLoops: Customer design program and research run beneath every phase.

roiMetrics.label: One AI Experience
roiMetrics.context: Consolidated naming, licensing and failure behaviors.

businessOutcomesAndROI.operationalSavings: Clear bar for experience quality before delivery.

leadershipTakeaway: Agentic UX requires turning complex technical autonomy trade-offs into reliable, trusted governance frameworks.

title: Generative AI Assistant: Defining the GenAI Experience
subtitle: From a GenAI vision in December 2022 to agentic capabilities and an agent marketplace
description: From a GenAI vision in December 2022 to agentic capabilities and an agent marketplace.
detailedSummary: When generative AI arrived in late 2022, the IT service and operations suite had no agreed experience model for it. I led early ideation, use case exploration, customer research, UX strategy and vision for GenAI capabilities. That direction became the foundation of the company’s GenAI features: summaries, insights, recommendations and conversation across workflows.
problemSpace: Lack of suite-wide experience model for GenAI when capabilities emerged in late 2022.
solution: Woven GenAI into the workflow: a capability model (summarise, surface insights, recommend, converse, create, aggregate) delivered in context.
keyOutcomes: Shared design language across ITSM and AIOps
role: UX leader for GenAI direction: ideation, use case exploration, customer research, UX strategy and vision
teamComposition: Six designers · Research: two UX researchers

leadershipPerspective.executiveMandate: Set the direction early, turn it into reusable patterns, and keep work grounded in customer evidence.
leadershipPerspective.strategicRole: Led end-to-end UX strategy, design audits, prototypes and recurring customer research.
leadershipPerspective.crossFunctionalSynergy: Collaborated with engineering leaders and design-system portfolio leads.
leadershipPerspective.teamLeadership: Directed six product designers and two UX researchers.
leadershipPerspective.orgTransformation: Transformed individual AI features into shared patterns in the design system.

phase1Discover.overview: Phase 1: Discover & Empathize — Use Case Exploration & Behavioural Data.
keyInsights: Assistant is needed across the journey, not only in chat.
Trust depends on accuracy and editable output.

phase2Define.coreProblemStatement: How might we bring generative AI into service and operations workflows so people get summaries and recommendations in context?
jobsToBeDone: Get a summary and related knowledge for a ticket.
Show likely cause and remediation steps.
phase2Define.mentalModelMisalignment: Organising AI around prompts and answers rather than in-task workflow steps.

phase3Ideate.northStarVision: GenAI woven into the workflow via a unified capability model in one design language.

architecturalShifts.to: Contextual GenAI summary boxes and insights
architecturalShifts.rationale: Ties AI directly to the user task.

strategicTradeOffs: Treated generated code as draft requiring human review.

phase4Prototype.validationApproach: Usability testing, remote interviews, prototype reviews and design audits.

phase5Implement.governanceFramework: Design patterns documented for all products with legal disclaimers.
phase5Implement.designSystemIntegration: Delivered assistant concept, controls, and components.
phase5Implement.continuousFeedbackLoops: Research and product-analytics behavior data tied to design.

roiMetrics.label: Company GenAI Story
roiMetrics.context: One coherent GenAI story across service and operations.

commercialBenefits: Faster remediation and better security posture.
businessOutcomesAndROI.operationalSavings: Estimated over 10,000 hours/year saved in IT, HR, and finance.

leadershipTakeaway: Defining a new technology experience requires early vision paired with rigorous, evidence-led pattern creation.

title: Data Management: Agentic AI for Database Operations
subtitle: Bringing expert-level diagnosis to database teams without removing human control
description: Bringing expert-level diagnosis to database teams without removing human control.
detailedSummary: The Data product line covers relational and hierarchical database solutions. As squads moved to agentic AI, I led UX direction for three use cases (deadlock log analyser, autonomous reorganisation, exception list), the web log-analysis experience replacing terminal-era workflows, and 2026 customer-event demonstrations.
problemSpace: Database diagnosis required rare expert knowledge and relied on cumbersome terminal-era workflows.
solution: Designed an AI insights panel next to a report grid, enabling log analysis, deadlock diagnosis, and phased autonomy from report-only to approval-gated action.
role: UX leader for Data product line: agentic AI use cases, log analysis, Assistant consistency and demos
teamComposition: Design lead for Data product line · Research: one UX researcher

leadershipPerspective.executiveMandate: Keep squads anchored on the customer problem, protect a consistent Assistant experience, and carry three agentic use cases.
leadershipPerspective.strategicRole: Guided problem framing, clarifying phase-one report-only boundaries and defining AI roles.
leadershipPerspective.crossFunctionalSynergy: Partnered with product managers and Data engineers, backing offline HTML demos to remove event connectivity risk.
leadershipPerspective.teamLeadership: Enabled designers to prototype agentic flows with AI-assisted tools.
leadershipPerspective.orgTransformation: Bridged terminal habits with modern web-based AI data visualization.

phase1Discover.overview: Phase 1: Discover & Empathize — Design-Partner Discovery & Terminal Workflow Study.

researchAnalytics.detail: Studied across relational and hierarchical databases.

keyInsights: Web experiences must respect terminal habits.

phase2Define.coreProblemStatement: How might we give every database team the judgement of their most experienced DBA?
jobsToBeDone: Deadlock and performance drift analysis with likely causes.
phase2Define.mentalModelMisalignment: Treating AI as immediate automation rather than phased human-approved assistance.

phase3Ideate.northStarVision: Report first, human approved: AI insights panel next to a report grid.

architecturalShifts.from: Terminal panels and raw log files
architecturalShifts.to: Web log-analysis tool with dataset visualisations
architecturalShifts.rationale: Removes terminal-skill barriers and makes patterns visible.

strategicTradeOffs: Kept phase one in report-only mode with strict limits on object lists.

phase4Prototype.validationApproach: AI-built prototypes, offline HTML demos for EMEA 2026 event, and stakeholder reviews.

phase5Implement.governanceFramework: Weekly AI-for-Data reviews with product managers and formal sign-offs.
phase5Implement.designSystemIntegration: Designs follow design system and shared Assistant principles.
phase5Implement.continuousFeedbackLoops: Monthly review tracking priority and UX allocation.

roiMetrics.label: Agentic Workflows
roiMetrics.context: Deadlock analysis, reorganisation and exception list UX-complete.

commercialBenefits: Early customer reaction and pipeline interest at EMEA 2026.
businessOutcomesAndROI.operationalSavings: Consistent Assistant experience across the suite.

leadershipTakeaway: Data UX transformation requires respecting expert terminal habits while introducing phased, trusted agentic intelligence.

title: AMI Assistant & Platform Experience
subtitle: One consistent, trustworthy AI front door across workflows and products
description: One consistent, trustworthy AI front door across workflows and products.
detailedSummary: AMI (Assistant & Management Interface) is the unified AI front door across the company’s enterprise portfolio. I led UX direction for the platform experience, multi-product Assistant consistency, agentic workflow integration, and design governance for the 2026 releases.
problemSpace: Multiple AI capabilities across different products risked fragmenting the user experience and eroding trust.
solution: A cohesive AI front door with consistent invocation patterns, transparent reasoning, and adjustable autonomy dials.
keyOutcomes: Unified AI experience across 4 product lines
role: UX leader for AMI platform strategy and cross-suite AI experience consistency
teamComposition: Four designers · Research: two UX researchers

leadershipPerspective.executiveMandate: Establish a unified AI experience that feels native across all products while maintaining rigorous trust and governance.
leadershipPerspective.strategicRole: Defined portfolio-wide AI interaction paradigms and governance rules.
leadershipPerspective.crossFunctionalSynergy: Bridged AI research, R&D engineering, and product management.
leadershipPerspective.teamLeadership: Mentored design leads across product suites.
leadershipPerspective.orgTransformation: Shifted product teams from isolated feature silos to a unified platform ecosystem.

phase1Discover.overview: Phase 1: Discover & Empathize — Cross-Product Workflow & Trust Mapping.

phase2Define.coreProblemStatement: How might we deliver a unified AI assistant experience across diverse enterprise products without cognitive friction?
jobsToBeDone: Interact with AI seamlessly across products.
phase2Define.mentalModelMisalignment: Treating AI as a standalone chatbot rather than an embedded capability.

phase3Ideate.northStarVision: One trustworthy AI front door with consistent invocation and graduated autonomy.

architecturalShifts.rationale: Ensures predictable, cohesive user mental models.

strategicTradeOffs: Standardized assistant chrome across diverse product contexts.

phase4Prototype.validationApproach: Interactive prototyping, user testing with 12 enterprise customers, and executive reviews.

phase5Implement.governanceFramework: Cross-suite design governance and component design system integration.
phase5Implement.designSystemIntegration: AMI components baked into enterprise design system.
phase5Implement.continuousFeedbackLoops: Continuous telemetry and customer advisory council reviews.

businessOutcomesAndROI.operationalSavings: Reduced redundant design and engineering effort.

leadershipTakeaway: Unified AI experiences require rigorous architectural governance and unwavering commitment to user trust.
